---
title: "Part 3 — Extending"
---

Part 3 covers extending a Pico beyond a single, isolated artifact. You will
give a Pico a cryptographic identity, connect Picos across meshes, separate
who a Pico is from what it may do, and prepare a Pico for portability
between execution environments.

These lessons are based on the Pico-to-Pico identity architecture introduced
in Pico Engine 1.6 and are designed to be completed in order after
[Part 1 — Foundations](../part-1/index.qmd) and
[Part 2 — Building](../part-2/index.qmd).

## Lessons

- [1. Pico Identity](01-pico-identity/index.qmd) — did:webvh as a Pico's
  public cryptographic identity and did:peer as relationship-specific
  identity.
- [2. Cross-Mesh Communication](02-cross-mesh-communication/index.qmd) —
  DIDComm, subscriptions as cryptographic relationships, and how parent/
  child communication differs from external relationships.
- [3. Trust and Authorization](03-trust-and-authorization/index.qmd) —
  keeping identity and authorization separate, channel policy, and the
  implications for Open Engineering rules and parsers.
- [4. Portability](04-portability/index.qmd) — what it takes to move a Pico
  between engines without losing who it is.

Each lesson follows the same page layout as the rest of the course — see the
[course overview](../index.qmd) for the full pattern.
